title: Legislative districts of Ifugao

{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Ifugao''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Ifugao]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mountain Province}} In 1917 the undivided [[Mountain Province]], of which Ifugao was a component sub-province, was provided representation in the [[Philippine Legislature]]. Pursuant to the Revised Administrative Code (Act No. 2711) enacted on March 10, 1917, the non-Christian-majority areas of the Philippines, which then included the Mountain Province, were to be collectively represented in the legislature's [[Philippine Senate|upper house]] by two senators from the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Twelfth District|12th senatorial district]], both appointed by the [[Governor-General of the Philippines|Governor-General]]. Three assembly members, also appointed by the Governor-General, were to represent the [[Mountain Province]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|chartered city]] of [[Baguio]] in the [[Philippine Assembly|lower house]] as a [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#1917–1935|single at-large district]].{{cite book|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 (Act No. 2711)|date=1917|publisher=Bureau of Printing|url=https://archive.org/stream/RevisedAdministrativeCodeOfThePhilippineIslandsOf1917/Revised%20Administrative%20Code%20of%20the%20Philippine%20Islands%20of%201917#page/n43/mode/2up|accessdate=February 4, 2017|format=Digitized Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 from the Presidential Museum and Library Collection, uploaded on February 15, 2016}} The residents of Ifugao and the rest of the Mountain Province only began electing representatives through popular vote in [[1935 Philippine general election|1935]] by virtue of Act No. 4203; the law provided the territorial coverage for each lower house representative district, while also abolishing the senatorial district system. The sub-province was then represented as part of the Mountain Province's [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#3rd District (defunct)|third district]].{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws Enacted by the Philippine Legislature, Acts No. 4203 to 4275|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1937|publisher=Bureau of Printing Office|page=5|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880830;view=1up;seq=133}} In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], the Mountain Province sent [[#At-Large (defunct)|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, district representation was restored to the pre-war setup: the sub-province of [[Ifugao]] remained part of Mountain Province's [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#3rd District (defunct)|third district]]. The enactment of Republic Act No. 4695 on June 18, 1966 made the sub-province of [[Ifugao]] into a full-fledged province.{{cite web|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno4695.html|date=June 18, 1966|accessdate=February 4, 2017|website=Chan Robles Law Library|author=Congress of the Philippines|title=Republic Act No. 4695 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao}} The new province began electing its separate representative starting in [[1969 Philippine general election|the next general election]]. Ifugao was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region II]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#1984–1986|one representative, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. It retained its lone [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional district]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|accessdate=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected its member to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Lone District == {{main|Ifugao's at-large congressional district}} *'''Population (2020)''': 207,498{{Cite web |url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx |title=Archived copy |access-date=2018-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313193111/http://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx |archive-date=2018-03-13 |url-status=dead }} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
